audit_findings.title: The 2025 owner-earnings anchor may retain a nonrecurring tax benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $33.189 million reported tax benefit, equal to 40.2% of the $82.5 million anchor; actual correction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially inflates anchor OE and every forecast year derived from it through an unsustainable negative tax charge.
audit_findings.evidence: The change in income tax expense for the year ended December 31, 2025 resulting in an income tax benefit compared to an income tax expense in 2024 was primarily due to increased stock compensation deductions and decreased pretax income.
audit_findings.explanation: The unusual tax benefit is demonstrated, but its retention in the OE calculation is unresolved. Because the filed benefit is large relative to the anchor, even partial retention could materially raise operating value.
audit_findings.action: Trace the 2025 OE tax calculation through current tax, deferred tax, stock-option deductions and cash taxes; then rerun all scenarios using a sustainable cash-tax charge if any benefit was retained.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may omit long-term marketable securities
audit_findings.magnitude: $236.451 million omitted, or $1.77 per fully diluted share; 16.8% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Understates the cash-and-securities bridge after related interest income was purged from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $532.4 million, consisting of cash and cash equivalents of $120.5 million and marketable securities of $411.9 million, compared to cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $603.2 million, consisting of cash and cash equivalents of $127.7 million and marketable securities of $475.5 million as of December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error: $111.039 million of cash plus $197.158 million of short-term securities equals the recorded $308.197 million bridge, leaving the filed $236.451 million of long-term marketable securities excluded. The omission materially changes stated intrinsic value, although correcting it alone would not close the gap to the $111.62 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the long-term securities are unrestricted and non-operating, then rerun the bridge with total cash and marketable securities of $544.648 million.

audit_findings.title: A material regulatory decision predates the valuation but is absent from the perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $47.564 million of filed Q2 2026 Lifyorli revenue; total valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes normalized OE, growth, launch spending, working capital and the business perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: We have also submitted an NDA for relacorilant as a treatment, in combination with the chemotherapy medication nab-paclitaxel, for patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer with a PDUFA date of July 11, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated and more advanced than the finding states: FDA approval occurred in March 2026, commercial sales began in April, and Lifyorli generated $47.564 million in Q2. A September 2026 valuation using a null perimeter and FY2025-only economics excludes a known operating business. Revenue is positive for value, while launch costs and working-capital requirements offset part of that benefit.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild normalized OE and growth using filed Lifyorli revenue, launch expenses and working-capital requirements, and explicitly include the approved oncology business in the perimeter before rerunning the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Generic entry could make the smooth growth scenarios structurally wrong
audit_findings.magnitude: First-half 2026 average Hypercortisolism Product price declined 2.1%, while revenue increased $21.842 million, or 6.2%; additional-entry effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A discontinuous loss of price or volume would reduce normalized OE and invalidate the smooth growth paths.
audit_findings.evidence: The availability of generic versions of Korlym from Sun or Hikma could materially harm our results of operations and financial condition.
audit_findings.explanation: Teva competition and the adverse appellate outcome are established, but filed first-half results do not yet demonstrate a structural earnings collapse. Sun or Hikma entry and its economic effect remain forward-looking. The risk warrants monitoring because additional launches could produce erosion exceeding the bear scenario's gradual 2% annual decline.
audit_findings.action: Obtain post-July 2026 launch status and monthly volume, market-share and realized-price data for each generic; reset normalized OE and rerun discontinuous-loss scenarios if erosion appears.

audit_findings.title: Known 2026 recurring commercial costs are not in the FY2025 anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: First-half 2026 SG&A increased $107.741 million, or 55.4%, year over year—130.6% of the $82.5 million anchor; sustainable portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Raises recurring operating expenses and lowers normalized OE before growth is applied.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect our selling, general and administrative expense to be higher in 2026 than in 2025 due to increased commercial and administrative activities to support our increased sales and marketing efforts.
audit_findings.explanation: The cost step-up is demonstrated in filed results, not merely forecast: first-half SG&A reached $302.252 million versus $194.511 million. Although some spending supports new Lifyorli revenue and may not recur at the same level, projecting directly from FY2025 OE without incorporating the sustainable 2026 cost structure can materially overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Separate recurring commercial infrastructure from temporary launch spending in first-half 2026 SG&A, incorporate associated Lifyorli economics, and rerun the valuation from a normalized 2026 run rate.

audit_findings.title: Unaccrued litigation and regulatory exposures may be claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Uninsured settlements, damages or penalties reduce the equity bridge; recurring defense costs reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: No such amounts are accrued as of December 31, 2025, nor have any contingent losses that are either material or probable arisen since that date.
audit_findings.explanation: The proceedings are demonstrated and expanded during 2026, including continuing antitrust cases, a served qui tam complaint and securities litigation. No loss contingency was accrued, and the record supplies neither a probable loss nor a reasonably estimable amount. Economic exposure therefore remains unresolved and materiality cannot be established from the filed numbers.
audit_findings.action: Review subsequent dockets, management and counsel loss ranges, insurance coverage and exclusions, indemnities, and identifiable defense spending; deduct any supportable expected uninsured liability and normalize recurring legal costs before rerunning.
